primary_gt.answer: 13.0x; prioritize smoke and gas health-exposure triage
primary_gt.canonical_stance: The 2015 Borneo CO spike was a peat-fire haze exposure signal, so health triage leads.
required_claims: El Nino dryness and peat fires drove smoke/haze and CO
high CO implies inhalation/public-health triage for exposed population
burn-scar-only mapping is secondary because dNBR support is insufficient
forbidden_claims: PM2.5, illness, deaths, burned area, or universal peak exposure inferred from the CO ratio
flood or cyclone operations as the leading priority
dNBR evidence sufficient for leading burn-severity mapping

key_values.event_name: 2015 Indonesian drought, peat fires and transboundary haze
key_values.anchor_notes: Compound chain of El Nino dryness, peat fires and regional smoke/haze.

point_weather_context.role: supporting dry-context diagnostic, not a hard scoring requirement for the CO ratio

weaker_priorities: direct burn-severity mapping as the leading response
acceptable_answer_variants: 13 times, thirteen-fold, or 13.0x for the ratio
air-quality health triage, smoke-exposure triage, inhalation-exposure triage, or public-health smoke response for the priority

criteria.name: Final ratio and priority
criteria.description: Gives 13.0x or an equivalent thirteen-fold ratio and identifies smoke and gas health-exposure triage as the leading priority.
criteria.partial_credit: Up to 2 points for the correct ratio without the priority, or up to 2 points for the correct priority with an incorrect or missing ratio.

criteria.name: Carbon monoxide extraction and calculation
criteria.description: Correctly uses 1,300 ppb divided by 100 ppb, includes ppb units or clear concentration wording, and rounds to one decimal place.
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for recognizing both values but making a minor arithmetic, rounding, or unit omission.

criteria.name: Peat-fire haze mechanism
criteria.description: Explains that El Nino dryness and peat combustion produced smoke/haze and abundant carbon monoxide, making inhalation exposure the relevant mechanism.
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for naming fires or haze without connecting dryness, peat, and carbon monoxide.

criteria.name: Cross-scale evidence linkage
criteria.description: Links the CO index to the wider event context, including available event-window dry context, regional haze or satellite smoke context, and population exposure without making auxiliary low-rain counts a hard requirement.
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for using only one or two supporting context elements, or for describing dry context qualitatively without exact low-rain counts.

criteria.name: Operational implication
criteria.description: Translates the index into realistic public-health triage actions or priorities rather than treating it as a purely descriptive atmospheric number.
criteria.partial_credit: 1-2 points for a generic health warning without an operational triage explanation.

criteria.name: Rejection of weaker interpretations
criteria.description: Explains why burn-scar-only mapping should not lead and why flood or cyclone response is not the best fit.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for rejecting only one weaker interpretation or doing so without a clear scientific reason.

criteria.name: Bounded concise answer
criteria.description: Provides the requested short format and avoids unsupported claims about casualties, PM2.5, exact burned area, or universal exposure to the peak CO value.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for mostly clear formatting with minor overstatement or missing caution.

supports: carbon monoxide was reported at about thirteen times the usual concentration
the event anchor identifies a drought, peat-fire, smoke and haze chain
available event-window dry-weather context supports the peat-fire mechanism
population exposure context makes smoke and gas triage operationally relevant
cautions: the ratio is not a PM2.5 concentration or illness count
the Sentinel-2 dNBR product lacks sufficient scenes for direct burn-severity mapping
the event context does not make flood rescue or cyclone operations the leading priority
